questions.text: Repeat Example 12.3 for V_{BE} = 0.65 V. (9.66660 = g' s u'y)

Consider a p-n-p bipolar transistor, uniformly doped in each region. Sketch the energy-band diagram for the case when the transistor is (a) in thermal equilibrium, (b) biased in the forward-active mode, (c) biased in the inverse-active region, and (d) biased in circuit with both the B-E and B-C junctions reverse biased.
Calculate the collector current for (i) V_be = 0.58 V, (ii) V_be = 0.65 V, and (iii) V_be = 0.72 V.

An npn bipolar transistor has the following base parameters: D_e = 22 cm²/s, x_e = 0.80 μm and n_b = 2 × 10^13 cm⁻³. (a) The collector current is to be I_c = 2 mA when biased at V_be = 0.60 V. What is the required cross-sectional area A_e?
Using the results of part (a), what is the value of β such that |I_c| = 5 mA?

Consider the transistor described in Problem 12.3. (a) For a common-base current gain of α = 0.980, determine the common-emitter current gain [note: β = α / (1 - α)]. (b) Determine the emitter and base currents corresponding to the collector currents determined in Problem 12.3.
Assume that an npn bipolar transistor has a common-emitter current gain of β = 100. (a) For a base current I_b = 4.2 μA and a collector current I_c = 0.625 mA, determine (i) β, (ii) α, and (iii) I_e.
Consider Figure 12.8. Assume V_CC = 3 V and V_CE = 0.65 V. (i) For R_C = 25 kΩ, plot I_C versus V_CE over the range 0.20 ≤ V_CE ≤ 3 V. (ii) At what value of I_C does V_CE = 0?

A uniformly doped silicon npn bipolar transistor at T = 300 K is biased in the forward-active mode. The doping concentrations are N_e = 8 × 10^17 cm⁻³, N_p = 2 × 10¹⁶ cm⁻³, and N_c = 10¹⁵ cm⁻³. (a) Determine the thermal-equilibrium values p_n0, n_b0 and p_n0. (b) For V_be = 0.640, calculate the values of n_i at x = 0 and p_n at x' = 0.

A silicon bipolar transistor at T = 300 K is uniformly doped and is biased in the forward-active mode. The doping concentrations are N_e = 5 × 10¹⁷ cm⁻³, N_p = 10⁶ cm⁻³, and N_c = 10¹⁵ cm⁻³. (a) Find the thermal-equilibrium values n_b0, p_n0, and n_c0. (b) Determine the values of p_n at x = 0 and at x' = 0.

Consider a silicon npn bipolar transistor at T = 300 K with uniform doping concentrations of N_e = 10^{18} cm^{-3}, N_a = 5 \times 10^{16} cm^{-3}, and N_c = 10^{16} cm^{-3}. Let D_e = 25 cm^{2}/s, x_b = 0.70 \mu m, and assume x_e < x_b. The transistor is operating in saturation with |I_c| = 125 A/cm^{2} and V_{ce} = 0.70 V. Determine (a) V_{bc}, (b) V_{ce(sat)}, (c) the #cm^{-2} of excess minority carrier electrons in the base region, and (d) the #cm^{-2} of excess minority carrier holes in the long collector. Let L_c = 35 \mu m.

An npn bipolar transistor at T = 300 K has uniform dopings of N_e = 10^{19} cm^{-3}, N_a = 10^{17} cm^{-3}, and N_c = 7 \times 10^{15} cm^{-3}. The transistor is operating in the inverse-active mode with V_{be} = -2 V and V_{ce} = 0.565 V. (a) Sketch the minority carrier distribution through the device. (b) Determine the minority carrier concentrations at x = x_b and x' = 0. (c) If the metallurgical base width is 1.2 \mu m, determine the neutral base width.

A uniformly doped silicon npn bipolar transistor at T = 300 K with dopings of N_e = 5 \times 10^{17} cm^{-3}, N_a = 10^{16} cm^{-3}, and N_c = 5 \times 10^{14} cm^{-3} is biased in the inverse-active mode. What is the maximum B-C voltage so that the low-injection condition applies?

(a) The following currents are measured in a uniformly doped npn bipolar transistor: I_{c} = 0.50 mA, I_{e} = 3.5 \mu A, I_{c} = 0.495 mA, I_{k} = 5.0 \mu A, I_{o} = 0.50 \mu A, I_{po} = 0.50 \mu A. Determine the following current gain parameters: (i) \alpha, (ii) \beta, (iii) \delta, (iv) \gamma, and (v) \rho. (b) If the required value of common-emitter current gain is \beta = 120, determine the values of I_{c}, I_{e}, and I_{k} to meet this specification assuming \gamma = \delta = \beta.

A silicon npn bipolar transistor at T = 300 K has a B-E cross-sectional area of A_{E} = 5 \times 10^{-4} cm^{2}, neutral base width x_{b} = 0.70 \mu m, a neutral emitter with N_{e} = 5 \times 10^{17} cm^{-3}, and uniform doping concentrations of N_{e} = 5 \times 10^{17} cm^{-3}, N_{p} = 10^{16} cm^{-3}, and N_{n} = 10^{15} cm^{-3}. Other transistor parameters are D_{e} = 15 cm^{2}/s, \tau_{e} = \tau_{b} = 5 \times 10^{-7} s, and \tau_{c} = 2 \times 10^{-6} s. The transistor is biased in the forward-active mode and the recombination factor is \beta = 0.995. Determine the collector current for (a) V_{be} = 0.550 V, (b) I_{B} = 0.80 \mu A, and (c) I_{E} = 125 mA.

Consider a uniformly doped npn bipolar transistor at T = 300 K with the following parameters: N_{e} = 10^{18} cm^{-3}, N_{a} = 5 \times 10^{16} cm^{-3}, N_{c} = 10^{15} cm^{-3}, D_{e} = 8 cm^{2}/s, D_{b} = 15 cm^{2}/s}, D_{c} = 12 cm^{2}/s, \tau_{e} = 10^{-8} s, \tau_{b} = 5 \times 10^{-7} s, \tau_{c} = 10^{-7} s, \alpha = 0.8, x_{b} = 0.7 \mu m. For V_{CE} = 0.60 V and V_{BE} = 0.55 V, calculate (a) the currents J_{b}, J_{e}, J_{c}, and J_{k} and (b) the current gain factors \alpha, \beta, \delta, \alpha, and \beta.
(c) Considering the results of part (b), what can be said about the recombination factor being the limiting factor in the common-emitter current gain?

(a) The recombination current density, J_{o}, in an npn silicon bipolar transistor at T = 300 K is J_{o} = 5 \times 10^{-5} A/cm^{2}. The uniform dopings are N_{e} = 10^{18} cm^{-3}, N_{s} = 5 \times 10^{16} cm^{-3}, and N_{c} = 10^{15} cm^{-2}. Other parameters are D_{e} = 10 cm^{2}/s, D_{b} = 25 cm^{2}/s, \tau_{e} = 10^{-6} s, and \tau_{b} = 10^{-7} s. Determine the neutral base width so that the recombination factor is \delta = 0.995 when V_{be} = 0.55 V. (b) If \delta remains constant with temperature, what is the value of \delta when V_{be} = 0.55 V for the case when the temperature is T = 400 K? Use the value of \delta determined in part (a).

(a) Plot, for a bipolar transistor, the base transport factor, \alpha_{T}, as a function of (x_{a}/L_{s}) over the range 0.1 < (x_{a}/L_{s}) < 1. Use a log scale on the horizontal axis. (b) Assuming that the emitter injection efficiency and recombination factors are unity, plot the common-emitter gain for the conditions in part (a). (c) Considering the results of part (b), what can be said about the base transport factor being the limiting factor in the common-emitter current gain?

(a) Plot the emitter injection efficiency as a function of the doping ratio, N_{b}/N_{e}, over the range 0.1 < N_{s}/N_{e} < 1. Assume that D_{e} = D_{b} = L_{e} = L_{b} and x_{e} = x_{b}. (Use a log scale on the horizontal axis.) Neglect bandgap narrowing effects. (b) Assuming that the base transport factor and recombination factors are unity, plot the common-emitter current gain for the conditions in part (a). (c) Considering the results of part (b), what can be said about the emitter injection efficiency being the limiting factor in the common-emitter current gain?

(a) Plot the recombination factor as a function of the forward-bias B–E voltage for 0.1 \leq V_{be} \leq 0.6. Assume the following parameters: D_{b} = 25 cm^{2}/s, D_{e} = 10 cm^{2}/s, N_{e} = 5 \times 10^{18} cm^{-3}, N_{b} = 1 \times 10^{17} cm^{-3}, N_{c} = 5 \times 10^{15} cm^{-3}, x_{b} = 0.7 \mu m, \tau_{e} = \tau_{b} = 10^{-7} s, J_{o} = 2 \times 10^{-9} A/cm^{2}. (b) Assuming the base transport and emitter injection efficiency factors are unity, plot the common-emitter current gain for the conditions in part (a). (c) Considering the results of part (b), what can be said about the recombination factor being the limiting factor in the common-emitter current gain?

The emitter in a BJT is often made very thin to achieve high operating speed. In this problem, we investigate the effect of emitter width on current gain. Consider the emitter injection efficiency given by Equation (12.35a). Assume that N_{e} = 100 N_{b}, D_{e} = D_{b} = L_{e} = L_{b}. Also let x_{b} = 0.1 L_{p}. Plot the emitter injection efficiency for 0.01 L_{e} \leq x_{e} \leq 10 L_{e}. From these results, discuss the effect of emitter width on the current gain.

Consider the geometry shown in Figure P12.42 and the device parameters given in Problem 12.42 except for the emitter width S. Determine the maximum value of S such that the ratio of electrons being injected into the base at x = S/2 compared to x = 0 is no less than 0.90.

(a) Show that, in thermal equilibrium, the electric field in the neutral base region is a constant. (b) Indicate the direction of the electric field. Does this electric field aid or retard the flow of minority carrier electrons across the base? (c) Derive an expression for the steady-state minority carrier electron concentration in the base under forward bias. Assume no recombination occurs in the base. (Express the electron concentration in terms of the electron current density.)

formulas.description: Esta fórmula representa a densidade de portadores de carga em um material semicondutor em função da distância a partir de uma superfície ou de uma região específica. Ela descreve como a densidade de portadores diminui exponencialmente à medida que nos afastamos de uma fonte ou de uma região onde esses portadores estão concentrados.

symbols.description: Representa a densidade de portadores de carga em uma posição x no material.
Representa a densidade de portadores de carga na posição inicial, ou seja, na superfície ou na região de origem.
Representa a distância a partir da posição inicial onde a densidade de portadores está sendo medida.
Representa o comprimento de penetração, que é a distância característica na qual a densidade de portadores diminui significativamente.

formulas.description: Esta fórmula representa a relação entre a densidade de portadores de carga em um ponto específico de um material semicondutor e a densidade de portadores de carga em um ponto de referência, permitindo entender como a densidade varia ao longo do material.

symbols.description: Representa uma quantidade que pode estar relacionada a uma propriedade física, como a absorção ou a atenuação em um material.
Representa a densidade de portadores de carga em um ponto de referência, geralmente na superfície ou em um ponto inicial do material.
Representa a densidade de portadores de carga em um ponto específico x dentro do material, permitindo comparar com a densidade no ponto de referência.
Representa a função logarítmica natural, que é usada para calcular a taxa de variação relativa entre duas quantidades.

questions.text: Consider a uniformly doped p silicon bipolar transistor with doping concentrations of N_e = 10^{18} \, \text{cm}^{-3}, N_b = 5 \times 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3}, and N_c = 2 \times 10^{18} \, \text{cm}^{-3}. The common-base current gain is α = 0.9930. Determine (a) B(V_{bc}), (b) B(V_{ce}), and (c) the emitter-base breakdown voltage. (Assume N = 3 for the empirical constant.)

A high-voltage silicon npn bipolar transistor is to be designed such that the uniform base doping is N_s = 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3} and the common-emitter current gain is β = 50. The breakdown voltage B(V_{ce}) is to be at least 60 V. Determine the maximum collector doping and the minimum collector length to support this voltage. (Assume N = 3.)

A silicon npn bipolar transistor is uniformly doped with N_e = 8 \times 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3}. The metallurgical base width is x_{b} = 0.50 \, \text{mm} with V_{be} = 0.0 \, \text{V}. (a) Determine the expected avalanche B–C breakdown voltage. (b) Calculate the value of V_{ce} at which punch-through occurs.

Consider an n silicon bipolar transistor with doping concentrations of N_e = 2 \times 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3} and N_c = 5 \times 10^{15} \, \text{cm}^{-3}, and with a metallurgical base width of x_{b} = 0.65 \, \text{um}. Let V_{ce} = 0.625 \, \text{V}. (a) Determine V_{ce} at punch-through. (b) Calculate the magnitude of the maximum electric field in the B–C space charge region at punch-through.

Design a uniformly doped silicon npn bipolar transistor so that \( \beta = 100 \) at \( T = 300 \) K. The maximum CE voltage is to be 15 V and any breakdown voltage is to be at least three times this value. Assume the recombination factor is constant at \( \delta = 0.995 \). The transistor is to be operated in low injection with a maximum collector current of \( I_c = 5 \) mA. Bandgap narrowing effects and base width modulation effects are to be minimized. Let \( D_{e} = 6 \) cm²/s, \( D_{s} = 25 \) cm²/s, \( \tau_{e} = 10^{-7} \) s, and \( \tau_{b} = 10^{-7} \). Determine doping concentrations, the metallurgical base width, the active area, and the maximum allowable \( V_{BE} \).

Design a pair of complementary npn and pnp bipolar transistors. The transistors are to have the same metallurgical base and emitter widths of \( W_{e} = 0.75 \) µm and \( x_{e} = 0.5 \) µm. Assume that the following minority carrier parameters apply to each: \( D_{n} = 23 \) cm²/s, \( \tau_{n} = 10^{-7} \) s, \( D_{p} = 8 \) cm²/s, \( \tau_{p} = 5 \	imes 10^{-8} \) s. The collector doping concentration in each device is constant at \( 6 \	imes 10^{18} \) cm⁻³ and the recombination factor in each device is constant at \( \delta = 0.9950 \). (a) Design, if possible, the devices so that \( \beta = 100 \) in each device. If this is not possible, how close a match can be obtained? (b) With equal forward-bias base-emitter voltages applied, the collector currents are to be \( I_{c} = 5 \) mA with each device operating in low injection. Determine the active cross-sectional areas.

standaloneFormulas.description: Esta fórmula representa a relação entre a corrente de polarização de um diodo e a tensão aplicada, levando em consideração a densidade de corrente de saturação e a tensão térmica. A fórmula é utilizada para calcular a eficiência de um diodo em conduzir corrente sob uma determinada tensão.
concepts: Efeito da temperatura na condução elétrica

symbols.description: Representa a eficiência ou a fração de corrente que passa através do diodo sob as condições dadas.
É a densidade de corrente de saturação do diodo, que é uma medida da corrente que flui através do diodo quando ele está reversamente polarizado.
Representa a densidade de corrente real que flui através do diodo sob a polarização direta.
É a tensão entre a base e o emissor em um transistor ou a tensão direta aplicada a um diodo.
É a tensão térmica, que é uma medida da energia térmica disponível para os portadores de carga em um semicondutor, geralmente dependente da temperatura.
